one_line: Demonstrates how chin augmentation alters the perception of nose size using interactive visual comparisons.

hook.what_happens: A split-screen slider compares a woman's face before and after, asking if her nose is too big.
hook.why_it_works: It challenges the viewer's visual perception and addresses a common cosmetic insecurity.

shots.description: Split-screen comparison of a woman's face with a slider moving across.
Heatmap overlay showing pixel changes on the face, accompanied by a bar chart.
Close-up analysis of the face highlighting the relationship between the nose and chin.
Text-based interactive prompt instructing the viewer to move their jaw.
Side-by-side comparison of the original and edited face.
Call to action screen with a search bar animation.

devices.name: split-screen slider
devices.what_it_is: A vertical line sliding horizontally to reveal before/after states.

devices.name: heatmap overlay
devices.what_it_is: Glowing color highlights on specific regions of the face.
devices.used_for: Showing exactly where image edits occurred.

devices.name: bar chart
devices.what_it_is: A simple vertical bar graph showing percentages.
devices.used_for: Quantifying pixel changes per facial feature.

devices.name: search bar mockup
devices.used_for: Directing users to search for the product.

onscreen_text.text: But it looks smaller in the second.
Almost none of it is on her nose.
When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose.
Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
Your nose just got smaller. You didn't touch it.
Not one feature. The whole face.
The question was never which feature to fix.
It's what the whole face does when one thing moves.
See it on your own face first.

transcript.text: Think your nose is too big?
Same woman, twice.
Same nose, both photographs.
But it looks smaller in the second.
Her chin is what moved.
Here is every pixel that changed.
Almost none of it is on her nose.
Your eye doesn't measure features.
It compares them.
When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose.
Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
Try it right now.
Push your lower jaw forward.
Your nose just got smaller. You didn't touch it.
The question was never which feature to fix.
It's what the whole face does when one thing moves.
See it on your own face first.
A preview, not a promise.
Search Refina AI.

narrative_arc: Hook the viewer by questioning their perception of nose size.
Reveal the optical illusion: only the chin was modified.
Provide data-driven proof using pixel-change analysis.
Explain the psychological mechanism of facial feature comparison.
Engage the viewer with a physical interactive test.
Introduce the product as a tool to preview these changes on their own face.

cta.what: Search Refina AI to preview facial adjustments on your own face.

subjects: Unidentified woman, serving as the visual model for the facial comparison.
what_makes_it_work: Uses a highly relatable physical illusion that viewers can test instantly.
Leverages data visualization to build scientific credibility.
Reframes cosmetic concerns from isolated features to overall facial harmony.

animations.name: SliderReveal
animations.what_moves: Vertical divider line and the underlying 'before'/'after' image states
animations.purpose: Demonstrates the subtle difference between before and after states of a chin augmentation.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing any two states of an image, like color grading or photo editing.

animations.name: TrimPath Callouts
animations.what_moves: Oval and circular dashed outlines around the chin and nose
animations.purpose: Draws immediate visual focus to the specific facial regions being discussed.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting key areas of interest on a product or diagram.

animations.name: Bar Chart Grow
animations.what_moves: Vertical bars representing pixel change percentages
animations.layered_with: Heatmap overlay fading on the face
animations.purpose: Quantifies which parts of the face actually changed, proving the nose was untouched.
animations.reusable_as: Displaying statistical data or feature comparisons dynamically.
animations.would_need_building: An animated bar chart component where bars scale up from zero with stagger.

animations.name: Animated Checklist
animations.purpose: Guides the user through an interactive physical test to prove the optical illusion.
animations.reusable_as: Displaying step-by-step instructions or feature lists.

animations.name: Diverge Panels
animations.what_moves: Two halves of the face sliding apart to reveal two full faces side-by-side
animations.purpose: Transitions from a single split-screen comparison to a full side-by-side comparison.
animations.reusable_as: Comparing two full-frame variations of a subject side-by-side.
animations.would_need_building: A panel transition that splits a central image and slides the halves outward to reveal two distinct full images.

animations.name: Search Typing
animations.what_moves: Text characters inside the search input field
animations.layered_with: Search icon and input box fade-in
animations.purpose: Simulates a user typing the brand name into a search engine for a clear call to action.
animations.reusable_as: Any search-based call to action or typing simulation.
animations.would_need_building: A text-typing effect with a blinking cursor inside an input field.

signature_moves: Diverge Panels to transition from split-screen to side-by-side
animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements fade in or draw on using clean vector paths.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Hard cuts or simple fades out of frame.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts between analytical diagrams and full-face views.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The central portrait alignment remains consistent across scenes.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Bursty, with moments of static analysis punctuated by sliding transitions.

what_we_should_steal: Diverge Panels transition for elegant split-to-dual image comparisons
SliderReveal with synchronized text labels for interactive product demos
